info.everywhere.title: Plain map
info.everywhere.what.1: Each picture is an animal from your binder, where it lives in the wild.
info.everywhere.what.2: A number means several animals: tap it to spread them out.
info.everywhere.more.1: Tap All animals to choose places, habitats and groups.
info.everywhere.more.2: Drag to spin the globe, pinch to zoom.
info.relief.what.1: The colours show how high and how dry the land is. Under the sea, light and dark shading shows the ridges and valleys of the sea floor.
info.relief.what.2: Slide to the Ice Age: the sea goes down and new land appears. The dashed line is today's coast. The sea fell because so much of its water was locked up in the ice.
info.relief.more.1: Taiwan's highest mountain, Yushan, is 3,952 m high.
info.forests.what.1: The coloured lines show where each kind of forest grows naturally. Press ▶ to watch the green come and go.
info.forests.more.1: Tropical forests are warm and wet all year. Northern forests have long, snowy winters.
info.reefs.what.1: Coral reefs grow in warm, shallow, clear seas.
info.reefs.what.2: The yellow sea is warm water. Press ▶ to see it move with the seasons.
info.reefs.more.1: The Great Barrier Reef in Australia is the biggest reef system on Earth.
info.reefs.more.2: Tiny algae living inside the corals need sunlight to make food.
info.night.what.1: The sun lights half of the Earth at a time: that half has day.
info.night.what.2: The lights are towns and cities at night.
info.night.more.1: The Earth turns once a day, so day and night go round and round it.
info.temp.what.1: Red is hot, blue is cold.
info.rain.what.1: The blues show how much rain falls in each month: the darker, the more.
info.rain.what.2: Press ▶ and watch the rainy belt move north and south with the seasons.
info.rain.more.1: Every summer the monsoon brings wet air from the sea to South and East Asia. In Taiwan, the plum rains come in May and June.
info.plants.what.1: The colours show how green the plants are in each month.
info.plants.more.1: When it is summer in Taiwan, it is winter in Australia, so their plants are green at different times of the year.
info.temp.what.2: On land: the ground by day. At sea: the top of the water.
info.temp.more.1: Sand warms up faster than water.
info.depth.what.1: The deeper the sea, the darker the blue.
info.depth.what.2: Sunlight only reaches the top 200 m.
info.depth.more.1: The deepest place is the Challenger Deep in the Mariana Trench: about 11,000 m.
info.plates.what.1: The Earth's outer shell is cracked into giant pieces called plates.
info.plates.what.2: The plates move very slowly, about as fast as your fingernails grow: a few cm a year.
info.plates.more.speed: The longer the arrow, the faster the plate moves.
info.plates.more.ring: More than half of the world's active volcanoes above the sea are around the Pacific Ocean: the Ring of Fire.
info.plates.bound.apart: Hot rock rises into the gap and makes new sea floor.
info.plates.bound.crash: One plate dives under the other, or both crumple up into mountains.
info.plates.bound.slide: The plates scrape sideways past each other, and the ground shakes.
info.plates.taiwan.1: Taiwan is where two plates meet: the Philippine Sea Plate and the Eurasian Plate are squeezing together by about 8 cm a year.
info.plates.taiwan.2: The push lifts Taiwan's tall mountains and causes its many earthquakes.
info.plates.taiwan.3: Taiwan has many hot springs. Near Taipei is the Tatun Volcano Group: when it last erupted is uncertain, and scientists watch it closely.
info.plates.taiwan.more: Scientists split the part of the Eurasian Plate next to Taiwan into smaller plates: the Yangtze and Sunda plates.
